key_insight: PlenopticDreamer synchronizes generative hallucinations across views and time so camera-controlled re-rendered video remains coherent in multi-view settings. It uses a plenoptic (multi-view) representation plus cross-view/time synchronization to lock stochastic generative outputs into consistent spatio-temporal content.
problem_solved: Addresses inconsistent, hallucinated content across multiple camera views and frames caused by the stochastic nature of generative video re-rendering models.
method: Build a plenoptic (multi-view) scene representation that conditions re-rendering on camera pose and shared scene latents.
Introduce a synchronization mechanism that aligns or shares generative hallucinations across views and time (e.g., shared latents / cross-view attention) to eliminate stochastic mismatches.
Enforce spatio-temporal coherence via alignment and consistency objectives inside the re-rendering pipeline so camera-controlled outputs remain stable and realistic.
impact: Makes camera-controlled generative video re-rendering viable for multi-view setups (VR/AR, multi-camera capture, view synthesis), improving realism and usability for downstream applications and research in controllable video generation.
visual_elements: Before/after multi-view frame grid showing inconsistent hallucinations vs synchronized consistent re-rendering
Architecture diagram: plenoptic field → synchronization module → renderer, with camera pose input
Temporal strip illustrating the same region across frames to show improved spatio-temporal coherence
Camera trajectory icon + output video frames to convey camera-controlled re-rendering
paper_authors: Xiao Fu, Shitao Tang, Min Shi, Xian Liu, Jinwei Gu
